item.description:
Your Mac's own microphone. The app now dictates through the Mac's built-in microphone whatever the system input is set to — a plugged-in headset or a headphone cable's remote no longer takes over without you knowing. Apple tunes that microphone for speech; it's the same on every MacBook; and it's never a Bluetooth headset's hands-free profile.

See which mic, and how quietly you can speak. Settings has a Microphone row with the mic's name on the line. Open it and a level bar follows your voice, with a mark at the quiet line. A dictation under that line gets a one-line hint afterwards: closer to the mic, or raise the input level.

Your sayings stay as you said them. "At the end of the day" no longer comes back as "by the end of the day" — fifty-eight common English sayings are kept exactly as spoken.

Also: the app pack spells Wispr Flow, and the minutes on every row line up.

Missed a release? 0.17.7 added a Web Design pack and taught the Coding pack JetBrains. 0.17.6 gave Flow an hour, took Breathe and Flow out of beta, added Control+Option+Backspace to delete what you just said, and made Redraft work after a quiet spell. 0.17.5 marked Draft and Prompt as beta and taught Prompt to keep your questions as questions. Every release, in order: github.com/richardgaston/dictation-releases/releases.
